investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T10:48–10:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for ~146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is characterized as an observability eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint rather than a confirmed user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible peer-pod nodes: existing running remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — peer-pod node pool is undersized for concurrent demand: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector, meaning the effective scheduling domain is very small and easily saturated.

TERTIARY — a prior eval run or user workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running that were not cleaned up, consuming VM slots that would otherwise be available. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup completed, slots may remain occupied.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the pod spec could be excluding nodes that do have capacity, but the scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' as the reason for the 2 eligible nodes, making a pure misconfiguration the less likely primary cause.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion prevents pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T10:51–10:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner from creating a remote agent at all, which means the probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905, createAgent call) never completes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for the eval probe's pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes. Even if VM capacity were freed, a misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could still block scheduling on the other 4 nodes.

Tertiary — eval probe pod resource request or priority class prevents preemption: the scheduler message states 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', suggesting either no lower-priority pods exist on the 2 eligible nodes or the incoming pod's priority is not high enough to trigger eviction.

Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: if the cluster autoscaler is configured to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, a delay in node provisioning could cause a temporary scheduling gap. No autoscaler evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T10:48–10:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for ~146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is characterized as an observability eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint rather than a confirmed user-facing outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible peer-pod nodes: existing running remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — peer-pod node pool is undersized for concurrent demand: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector, meaning the effective scheduling domain is very small and easily saturated.

TERTIARY — a prior eval run or user workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running that were not cleaned up, consuming VM slots that would otherwise be available. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup completed, slots may remain occupied.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the pod spec could be excluding nodes that do have capacity, but the scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' as the reason for the 2 eligible nodes, making a pure misconfiguration the less likely primary cause.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector rules. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~146 s), causing all three remote-agents checks to fail before any agent lifecycle work begins. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=150036, endedAt=2026-07-06T10:51:06.496Z — the earliest check in the sequence also failed with the same cause.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduling error (145s stuck), latencyMs=149390, endedAt=2026-07-06T10:53:35.886Z — confirms the capacity condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150791, status=fail — the probe waited the full scheduler timeout before giving up, consistent with a hard capacity ceiling rather than a transient blip.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence fields were collected at all, confirming the agent pod never started and the runner never reached createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with probe termination at the scheduling stage before any API call succeeded.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this call is never reached when pod scheduling fails upstream.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules at all, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is artificially constrained. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — kata-containers / peer-pods daemon capacity not scaled to match eval concurrency: the three checks ran sequentially (ending at 10:51, 10:53, 10:56) and each independently exhausted capacity, suggesting the VM resource pool was not replenished between runs.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable error if capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three should reproduce the kata.peerpods.io/vm Insufficient error if the capacity condition persists.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and check the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource allocatable vs. requested values.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the affected nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads are holding VM slots to determine whether any are stale, leaked, or eligible for eviction.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire remote-agent provisioning path is blocked.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false. degradedAfterFailures=1 means the feature is already in degraded state.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that match pod affinity, meaning the VM slot resource is fully consumed.
affectedAreas.details: This is an infrastructure-layer constraint, not an application code defect.

affectedAreas.label: Pod node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially limiting the schedulable pool to 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity exhaustion impact.
affectedAreas.details: If the affinity rules are correct, the fix is capacity expansion. If they have drifted, correcting them could expose additional schedulable nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The createAgent() call at line 1918 is never reached because the pod scheduling failure surfaces before the runner can collect any evidence, causing a total contract miss.
affectedAreas.details: Lines 1913-1918 in run-status-probes.mjs define the probe entry point.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes to confirm exhaustion and identify which pods are holding slots.

Check for stale or leaked remote-agent pods (Completed, Error, or Terminating phase) that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations without doing useful work, and evict or delete them to free capacity.

Verify that the node affinity/selector rules for remote-agent pods are correct and that no node labels have drifted — if 4 of 6 nodes are excluded unintentionally, restoring labels would expand the schedulable pool.
If capacity is legitimately exhausted by active workloads, coordinate with the infrastructure team to increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota or add nodes with peer-pods support to the cluster.

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm recovery and establish a passing baseline (lastPassingAt is currently null, meaning no historical pass exists in the eval history).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all 6 nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the VM extended resource is exhausted and on which nodes, proving or disproving the capacity-ceiling hypothesis.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Focus on the 2 nodes that match pod affinity to see current allocation.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm to identify stale or leaked holders
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, node: .spec.nodeName, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether VM slots are held by running, completed, or leaked pods, which determines whether eviction or cleanup can restore capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Look for pods in Completed or Error phase that may not have released their resource allocation.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the failing remote-agent pod to confirm scheduler rejection details
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Surfaces the exact scheduler events and resource requests for the pending pod, confirming the kata.peerpods.io/vm request amount and the affinity rules in effect.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Cross-reference node affinity rules against current node labels to check for label drift.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the failed expected-output contract after any capacity remediation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether restoring VM capacity resolves the scheduling failure and allows the eval to collect the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: A passing run would produce all 5 required evidence fields and satisfy the message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' assertion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Review node labels on all 6 nodes to validate affinity/selector rules
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity rules are correctly excluded or whether label drift has reduced the schedulable pool below intended size.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: If labels are missing or incorrect, restoring them could expand the schedulable pool from 2 to a larger set.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed, the scheduling error message would be misleading and another cause (e.g., a quota policy or admission webhook) would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on the next run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly leaked pod that was GC'd) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass, the root cause would be localized to the runtime probe's specific pod spec rather than a cluster-wide VM capacity issue.

If a passing run of any remote-agents check is found in history (lastPassingAt is currently null due to no previous run data), it would establish a baseline and help determine whether this is a regression or a first-time capacity ceiling.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout inside the agent lifecycle eval.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check eval that submits a dry-run pod (kubectl apply --dry-run=server) with the remote-agent spec and asserts it is schedulable, catching node affinity drift and resource exhaustion before the full agent creation probe runs.

Add a stale-pod cleanup eval that detects remote-agent pods in terminal phases (Completed, Error, Terminating) that are still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, alerting before capacity is fully consumed.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so future failures include machine-readable scheduling diagnostics rather than only a timeout message.
